title: Separable differential equations & slope fields
examples: How do I know when to use separation of variables?
What is the difference between a general and a particular solution?
Can slope fields help me find the actual curve?

explain.say: Today we look at separable differential equations. These equations can be separated into two parts. We move all the y terms with dy, and all the x terms with dx. For example, if we have dy by dx equals x times y. We move y to the left and x times dx to the right. So we get dy by y equals x times dx. This sets up the separation.

Next, we integrate both sides of the separated equation. Remember to add the constant of integration, which we call c. Integrating dy by y gives us the natural logarithm of the absolute value of y. Integrating x times dx gives us x squared divided by two. So we get the equation ln of the absolute value of y equals x squared divided by two plus c. This is the general solution.

To find a particular solution, we use an initial condition. If we are given that y equals two when x equals zero. We substitute these values into our general solution. So we get the natural logarithm of two equals zero squared divided by two plus c. This lets us solve for the specific constant c.

Slope fields show the slope at many points. Each point has a little line segment showing the slope. For the equation dy by dx equals x times y, at the point one, two, one, the slope is one times two, which is two. This gives a visual picture of the function's behavior.

faq.q: What does it mean to solve for a general solution?
faq.a: It means finding the family of all possible curves that fit the equation. You keep the constant of integration, c, in your final answer. You might also hear this called finding the general form.
asks: What is the general form of the solution?
How do I leave the constant in the answer?

faq.q: When should I use separation of variables?
faq.a: You use it when the right side of the differential equation can be written as a product of a function of x and a function of y. Look for the form f(x)g(y).
asks: Does the equation have to be a product?

faq.q: How do I find the particular solution?
faq.a: You must use the given initial condition, like y equals three when x equals one. You plug these numbers into the general solution to find the single value for c. This locks the curve in place.
asks: What do I do with the initial values?
Do I plug the values into the original equation?

faq.q: What does the slope field represent?
faq.a: It is a graph showing the slope of the solution curve at many different points. It does not show the curve itself, just the direction everywhere.
asks: Is the slope field the graph?
What does the slope field tell me?

faq.q: Can I use the slope field to find the exact equation?
faq.a: No, the slope field only gives you an approximation of the curve's path. You usually need to solve the equation analytically to find the exact function.
asks: Can I graph it from the slope field?
Is the slope field a solution?

facts: A differential equation relates a function to its derivatives. The derivative is represented by dy by dx.
Separable equations are those where dy by dx can be written as f(x)g(y).
After separation, you integrate both sides independently to solve for the general solution.
A particular solution is found by using an initial condition to solve for the constant c.

quiz.say: If dy by dx equals x over y, what is the separated form?
quiz.show: dy/dx = x/y => y dy = x dx
quiz.why: You must multiply by y and dy to get y dy on the left side.

wrong.0: This leaves the equation in differential form instead of separated.
wrong.1: This leaves an extra dy term that does not belong.
wrong.3: This incorrectly moves the x to the left side.

quiz.say: What is the general solution for dy by dx equals 3y x?
quiz.why: Integrating both sides correctly yields the natural log form with the constant.

wrong.0: You cannot simply remove the natural logarithm function.
wrong.1: You forgot to divide the x^2 by two when integrating.
wrong.2: While mathematically related, the standard form keeps the log separated from the constant.

quiz.say: For dy by dx equals y over x, if y equals 2 when x equals 1, what is the value of C?
quiz.why: Plugging in y equals 2 and x equals 1 gives ln(2) equals ln(1) plus C, so C equals ln(2).

wrong.0: You incorrectly assumed the constant must be the y-value.
wrong.1: You might have incorrectly set ln(1) to zero and ignored the y-value.
wrong.2: This is correct, but the simplest form is just ln(2) since ln(1) is zero.
